name: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way

meta.wiki: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way

summary: In the bustling halls of Ironforge, the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle seeks to uncover the evolutionary secrets of Azeroth by studying oozes and slimes. Curious about the Royal Apothecary Society's strange fascination with these vile puddles, he tasks Alliance adventurers with journeying to tainted Felwood to bottle up specimen samples.

sections.title: A Peculiar Obsession
sections.body: While most scholars of the Explorers' League concern themselves with ancient titan relics or buried dwarven genealogies, Laris Geardawdle has set his inquisitive mind on a squelchier subject: oozes. Ubiquitous across wetlands, cursed woods, and damp ruins, these living puddles defy standard biological classification. Having witnessed Forsaken apothecaries scooping up slime samples across Lordaeron, Laris has resolved to understand what makes these gelatinous horrors so uniquely interesting to the Undercity's alchemists.

sections.title: The Primordial Secretion
sections.body: Laris harbors a controversial theory that oozes are not mere unnatural vermin or magical byproducts, but primordial secretions intimately tied to the planetary genesis of Azeroth itself. To prove this hypothesis, he dispatches brave scouts across the ocean into the blighted canopy of Felwood to capture specimens of Cursed and Tainted Oozes in specially crafted jars.

sections.title: Proving Gnomish Worth
sections.body: Behind Laris's academic pursuit lies a deeply personal motivation shared by many of his displaced kin. Following the devastating radioactive fall of Gnomeregan, thousands of gnomes found sanctuary as refugees within the Great Forge of Ironforge. By securing a breakthrough discovery for the Explorers' League, Laris hopes to silence dwarven skeptics and affirm that welcoming gnomes into the mountain city was no act of simple charity, but an enduring asset to Alliance science.

faq.answer: Laris Geardawdle is a gnomish researcher and scholar residing in Ironforge. Working alongside the Explorers' League, he dedicates himself to understanding the biological origins of oozes and slimes across Azeroth.

faq.q: Why does Laris care so much about ooze?
faq.answer: Laris suspects that oozes may be tied to the planetary origin of Azeroth as primordial secretions. Additionally, noticing that the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society aggressively harvests slime samples has made him eager to unravel their secret properties before the Horde does.

faq.q: Where do you gather the ooze samples?
faq.answer: The samples must be gathered from Cursed Oozes and Tainted Oozes wandering the corrupted forests of Felwood in northern Kalimdor, using empty glass containers provided by Laris.

faq.q: Why are the Forsaken collecting oozes?
faq.answer: The Royal Apothecary Society routinely experiments with toxins, blights, and biological horrors to advance Forsaken alchemy. Their interest in raw oozes signals to Alliance scholars that the creatures harbor virulent or mutagenic compounds.

faq.q: How does this quest connect to the fall of Gnomeregan?
faq.answer: Laris feels the pressure of being a refugee in Ironforge after Gnomeregan's loss to troggs and radiation. He believes that securing a major scientific triumph for the Explorers' League will prove that granting asylum to gnomes was truly worthwhile for the dwarven hosts.

faq.q: What happens after you deliver the samples?
faq.answer: Laris immediately begins testing the specimens in his laboratory setup in Ironforge, further developing his theories regarding ooze taxonomy and elemental origins.

angles.text: Laris embodies the relentless intellectual drive of gnomes rebuilding their reputations and pride after the heartbreaking loss of Gnomeregan.
Though traditional dwarven excavators favor stone and metal over gelatinous sludge, the Explorers' League nonetheless benefits from Laris's eccentric drive.
Monitoring the Royal Apothecary Society's gathering habits gives the Alliance vital intelligence on what sinister brews the Undercity may be concocting.
